$FG,14$$TX+CX,"HOLYC"$$FG$
$HL$
HolyC is C with the ceremony removed. A bare string is a
print. There is no $FG,12$main()$FG$. Every line is both script and
source, and the shell is the compiler.

$TR,"THE ONE THING TO TRY FIRST"$
A statement that is only a string prints it:

$FG,11$  "HELLO, TEMPLE.\n";$FG$

Type that into the terminal. It compiles and runs.
$TR-$

$TR,"TYPES"$
$FG,10$  U0$FG$   nothing
$FG,10$  I64$FG$  a signed 64 bit integer
$FG,10$  F64$FG$  a double
$FG,10$  U8$FG$   a byte, and a character
$TR-$

$TR,"CALLING WITHOUT PARENTHESES"$
The signature move. A function name on its own line is a
call. These two are the same thing:

$FG,11$  GodWord;
  GodWord();$FG$

That is why the shell and the language are one program.
$TR-$

$TR,"WHAT THIS MACHINE UNDERSTANDS"$
I64 / F64 / U0 declarations, assignment, arithmetic,
comparison, && and ||, if / else, while, for, {} blocks,
function definitions, and calls with or without parens.
Built in: Print, GodWord, GodDoodle, GodSong, Beep,
BellRing, Sleep, Rand, RandU16, StrLen, Cd, Dir, MemSet,
Panic, Exit.
$TR-$

$MA,"RUN A LOOP",LM="I64 i; for (i=0;i<7;i++) \"DAY %d\\n\", i;"$
$MA,"ASK GOD FOR A WORD",LM="GodWord;"$

$SP,"temple"$$FG,14$ TempleOS V5.03$FG$
$FG,7$Public domain. God's third temple.$FG$
$HL$
$FG,11$This document is DolDoc.$FG$ Sprites sit inside the line.
Colours are commands. Links are commands. So are buttons.
Press $FG,14$[SRC]$FG$ on the title bar to see what it is made of.

$TR,"THE DESKTOP"$
$SP,"folder"$ Double click to open. Drag icons anywhere.
Drag on bare desktop to rubber band a group.
Right click for the menu.
$TR-$

$TR,"WHERE TO GO"$
$SP,"cross"$ $LK,"Charter.DD",A="FI:::/Doc/Charter.DD"$ why this is 100,000 lines
$SP,"scroll"$ $LK,"DolDoc.DD",A="FI:::/Doc/DolDoc.DD"$ this format, explained
$SP,"disk"$ $LK,"HolyC.DD",A="FI:::/Compiler/HolyC.DD"$ the language
$SP,"bell"$ $LK,"Hardware.DD",A="FI:::/Doc/Hardware.DD"$ the monitor and the panel
$SP,"flame"$ $LK,"Demo",A="FI:::/Demo"$ things that run
$SP,"ark"$ $LK,"Home",A="FI:::/Home"$ yours: notes, a temple, a covenant
$SP,"glider"$ $LK,"Kernel",A="FI:::/Kernel"$ ring 0, and what it does when it falls
$TR-$

$TR,"THINGS TO TRY"$
$MA,"GodWord",LM="GodWord;"$ ask for a word
$MA,"Neofetch",LM="NEOFETCH"$ the specs
$MA,"AfterEgypt",LM="AFTEREGYPT"$ the game
$MA,"Tasks",LM="TASKS"$ Adam, Seth, and the rest
$MA,"Lines",LM="LINES"$ how far over the Charter this machine is
$MA,"Panic",LM="PANIC"$ ring 0 has no safety net
$TR-$

$FG,8$640K. 16 colours. One voice. No network.$FG$

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"DOLDOC"$$FG$
$HL$
Every document on this machine is a program that draws
itself. A command sits between two dollar signs and takes
effect where it stands. To show a command instead of
running it, double its dollar signs: $$$$FG,14$$$$ is how
$$FG,14$$ is written down here.

$TR,"COMMANDS THIS BUILD UNDERSTANDS"$
$FG,11$  $$FG,N$$$FG$        set the ink to VGA colour N, 0..15
$FG,11$  $$BG,N$$$FG$        set the paper
$FG,11$  $$FG$$$FG$          back to normal
$FG,11$  $$SP,"name"$$$FG$   drop a sprite into the line
$FG,11$  $$LK,"t",A="FI:path"$$$FG$  a link to a file or a folder
$FG,11$  $$MA,"t",LM="cmd"$$$FG$     a button: HolyC, or any word the terminal knows
$FG,11$  $$TR,"t"$$ ... $$TR-$$$FG$   a collapsible tree
$FG,11$  $$HL$$$FG$          a rule across the page
$FG,11$  $$TX+CX,"t"$$$FG$   centre a line
$FG,11$  $$BK,1$$..$$BK,0$$$FG$ blink, because it is 1996
$FG,11$  $$UL,1$$..$$UL,0$$$FG$ underline
$FG,11$  $$ID,n$$$FG$        indent by n
$FG,11$  $$$$$FG$           a literal dollar sign
$TR-$

$TR,"THE SPRITES ON HAND"$
$SP,"temple"$ temple   $SP,"cross"$ cross   $SP,"folder"$ folder
$SP,"scroll"$ scroll   $SP,"disk"$ disk    $SP,"bell"$ bell
$SP,"flame"$ flame    $SP,"ark"$ ark     $SP,"glider"$ glider
$SP,"god"$ god      $SP,"note"$ note
$TR-$

$TR,"TRY ONE"$
$MA,"A BELL, SEVEN TIMES",LM="BellRing(7);"$
$MA,"A WORD FROM GOD",LM="GodWord;"$
$MA,"THE TASKS WINDOW",LM="TASKS"$
$TR-$

$FG,12$$BK,1$This is the part you cannot do anywhere else.$BK,0$$FG$

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"THE CHARTER"$$FG$
$HL$
The specification was a size. 100,000 lines, and not one
more, for the whole operating system: kernel, compiler,
editor, graphics, games and documentation together.

A modern kernel alone is around thirty million.

$FG,11$Type $FG,14$LINES$FG,11$ in the terminal to audit this one
against the same budget.$FG$

$MA,"COUNT THE LINES",LM="LINES"$

$FG,8$A limit is not a shortage. It is a decision about what
is allowed to be complicated.$FG$

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"HOLYTRON DM-640"$$FG$
$HL$
The case is the page. It grows with the window.

$TR,"THE CHIN"$
$FG,11$SCAN$FG$     line pitch of the glass. OFF is a picture with no lines.
$FG,11$DGAUSS$FG$   a switch. On, the tube shows the faint patches of
         the wrong colour a magnetised tube shows toward its
         corners. $MA,"FIRE THE COIL",LM="DEGAUSS"$
$FG,11$PHOS$FG$     phosphor persistence. P1 is fast, P7 smears.
$FG,11$BURN$FG$     twenty years of the same menubar.
$FG,11$POWER$FG$    really works. The set is off whenever the app opens.
$TR-$

$TR,"THE PANEL"$
$FG,11$MUS$FG$ and $FG,11$SFX$FG$ are pots. Drag them round, scroll, or
use the arrow keys. Ten detents each. Both start at 0.

$FG,11$VHLD$FG$ and $FG,11$HHLD$FG$ are the hold controls. They start
locked at 5. Take one off centre and the picture goes
with it, exactly like the set your grandmother hit.

$FG,11$LOBBY$FG$ is the music switch. It keeps playing over the
desktop, not just the splash.

The clicks the panel makes are not routed through SFX.
Plastic does not have a volume knob.
$TR-$

$TR,"AT BOOT"$
Hold $FG,14$DEL$FG$ while the machine powers up. POST stops where it
is and opens $FG,11$BIOS SETUP$FG$: four screens, arrow keys to move,
+ and - to change a value, F9 for the defaults, F10 to keep what
you changed and boot again, ESC to leave it. Four things in it
change the next power-on: the POST speaker, the memory test, a
hold on the BIOS screen for a slow hand, and the tube warm-up.
After eight hours away the cold start runs in full whatever
SETUP says.

$MA,"OPEN THE SAME SCREEN HERE",LM="CMOS"$
$TR-$

$FG,14$NOTES ON THE MACHINE$FG$
$HL$
640x480. 16 colours. One voice.
No network. No ads. No permission asked of anyone.

The compiler is the shell.
The shell is the editor.
The editor is the OS.

$FG,11$Press [SRC] on the title bar and type over this. It saves itself.$FG$
$FG,8$Press [DOC] and it draws itself again.$FG$

$SP,"ark"$ $FG,14$AN OFFERING OF 640 KILOBYTES$FG$
$HL$
It is enough. It was always enough.
The rest was decoration.

$MA,"RING THE BELL",LM="BellRing(7);"$
$MA,"RUN THE LOOP",LM="I64 i; for(i=0;i<7;i++) \"%d\\n\", i;"$

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"RING 0"$$FG$
$HL$
There is one ring and everything runs in it. No user mode,
no process isolation, no permission checks, no system call
boundary to cross. Any code can touch any byte.

That is not an oversight. It is the whole design: a single
address space is why the compiler can be the shell and why
a document can be a program.

$FG,12$It also means there is nothing to catch a fault.$FG$
A bad pointer does not raise an exception for somebody
else to handle. It drops you into the debugger, where you
were always going to end up anyway.

$TR,"WHAT IS IN THIS FOLDER"$
$LK,"Panic.HC",A="FI:::/Kernel/Panic.HC"$  the handler. Open it and press [RUN], or right-click it: RUN IT.
$MA,"BREAK SOMETHING",LM="PANIC"$ the same thing, from here.
$TR-$

$TR,"WHO IS RUNNING"$
$SP,"terminal"$ $MA,"TASKS",LM="TASKS"$ Adam, Seth and every window: end any of them but the first two.
$SP,"disk"$ $MA,"DEFRAG",LM="DEFRAG"$ the disk, moved cluster by cluster.
$SP,"temple"$ $MA,"NEOFETCH",LM="NEOFETCH"$ what the machine says about itself.
$TR-$

$SP,"cross"$ $FG,14$START HERE$FG$
$HL$
$LK,"Doc/Welcome.DD",A="FI:::/Doc/Welcome.DD"$ is the front door.

$FG,11$Or just open a Terminal and type$FG$ $FG,14$HELP$FG$$FG,11$.$FG$
